title: The Rider and the Horses of the Soul
english: His dwelling-place. For he says, 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion.' And since these things are established not by our power but by the grace of God, the word attributes to Him the cause of peace, saying: 'There He crushed the powers of bows, the shield and the sword and war' (Ps 75:5-7). For peace prevails in the place of God once the rulers of bows are crushed, from whom the evil one, sending his flaming arrows, was making afflictions and disordered movements, of which he was the cause. Along with the aforementioned bows, the related shield and sword are also crushed, and along with them, those called war are crushed; for the Lord is the one crushing wars (Ps 75:5-7).

And the holy men, looking ahead eternally, namely the unseen and eternal things, from which God illuminates differently the light of the knowledge of Christ—first before the manifestation through prophets and Moses, and after this through apostles and evangelists, so that those being illuminated become light, as Paul says: 'The God who said, Let light shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God' (2 Cor 4:6). And He marvelously added to the illuminating, that which He promises as knowledge to others, and by this God illuminates more paradoxically into knowledge and wisdom for the holy ones through both revelations and visions, seeing marvelously from the things mentioned. And even if it is not in Judea, as the Scripture says, these high contemplations and the doctrines of godliness are seen, and from these God marvelously illuminates those coming into the knowledge of truth. Often in the Scripture, intelligible things and angels are seen, from which God again illuminates, sending them into service for those about to inherit salvation. And to each of the editions it will be fitting [to say]: 'Draw near to the eternal things, protected by God for those who desire godliness, benefiting the prudent through the virtue of the present.' For understanding is a good thing for all who practice it. The senseless are troubled by both afflictions and wickedness; they are also troubled by both sensible and invisible deceivers, according to the [scripture]: 'Their senseless heart was darkened.' For to be darkened and to be troubled are the same; for each denotes ignorance, with the mind being darkened in both cases. And God is called the Jacob of the ascetic and man...

A good and righteous [state] is maintained against the reproach of one falling from these through personal laziness, being established by reproof. For some say that bodies are like vehicles and horses of the souls. In these horses, those riding them pleasure-lovingly desire the beginning of sleep, being drawn into a false breath of those who inhale the body and enslave it with skill, those sitting upon the horses.

Indeed, one sees in the Scripture the rider as being mostly falsely named, as also in Zechariah the prophet there is a threat of God: 'And I will strike every horse in ecstasy and the rider in thoughtlessness' (Zechariah 11:7); and according to Moses, a horse and a rider was thrown into the sea—and riders being praised. For instance, toward Elijah, Father Elisha, the army of Israel and his rider; and toward the Savior it is announced: 'Ride upon your horses, and your riding is salvation' (Psalm 75:8).

No one among the wretched is able to stand against God when He is angry, creating fear for those being judged, so that they might not overlook the One who knows the heart (Psalm 75:7). For those having the word toward Him as toward a judge say: 'Lord, Lord, if He observes iniquity, who will stand?' Moreover, even if no one will be able to stand against His wrath, being terrible, yet He Himself, through the coming goodness with mercy, judges. For mercy and judgment are yours, Lord.

Judgment listens from heaven, making everything happen according to the word of providence for the benefit of each. This agrees with what is in the prophecy of Amos: 'The Lord doing judgment, He has set high judgment and righteousness in the earth' (Amos 5:24). For as it is in heaven, He does all judgment in the high place; and as He listens from heaven, sending judgment from it to those on earth, He has set righteousness in the earth as the end of judgments (Psalm 75:11).

The hidden thing of man is in the mind. He who cleanses this will confess to God with gladness. Then he will celebrate in doing what is profitable, and he will be able to think the truths. If, however, 'He will confess' denotes the disclosure of sins, the understanding of the matter will be this: since the one desiring to be perfectly holy must not cleanse himself in solitary acts and words alone, he must confess while rebuking himself regarding a very brief thought. title: Authenticity of Voice and the Guarding of the Heart
english: He is able to be made manifest from [the prayer], 'Cleanse me from my secret sins.' If one does not even imply something regarding the non-existence [of sin], a confession might not occur; consequently, the remnant of the man's inner mind is celebrated having been found outside of all evil. Or, when the doubt concerning him is taken away by the manifestation of purity, the saint celebrates—not sometimes and sometimes not, but steadily and always knowing the truth and acting according to righteousness. For this is truly the feast according to the apostle who said, 'Let us celebrate, not in leaven of malice and wickedness, but in unleavened bread of sincerity and truth' (1 Cor 5:8).

He is terrible before the kings of the earth, who struck down Pharaoh, and pursued Nebuchadnezzar of men, altering his thinking as if his life were among beasts (Ps 76:13); he deprived Saul of the spirit, who, despising the covenant of God, [was rejected by] Samuel; for it is said, 'The Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul' (1 Sam 16:14), and he was oppressed by an evil spirit from the Lord, sent upon him by judgment and vote. And if even concerning ecclesiastical leaders these things are to be considered, hold fast to the God-breathed Scripture. For Paul, having called the elders of Miletus, says to them, 'Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock in which the Holy Spirit of God has made you overseers, and with Him, and also from among yourselves some will arise speaking twisted things, that is, the divine Spirit of the terrible ones being taken away' (Acts 20:28-30).

When the one speaking has departed far off, speaking with a strained voice (Ps 76:2). Since, therefore, the begotten essence is separated from the One who made [all], a cry according to the intellect is necessary. He is called God because He made all things, and Lord because He rules over those things which come from Him. And it is said, God indeed the Father, and Lord the Son. But to the one speaking, the day is one of affliction, his whole life, indeed, the age which has come upon him, in which he seeks God as one would seek a physician for a disease, calling out. He seeks [Him] through deed and disposition, not being deceived like those who are ignorant of the end regarding circumstances, just as Saul went to a medium and was deceived. But the saint, who is not troubled, seeks God in the night called the ignorance of circumstances, according to the...

According to Isaiah, my soul became attached to a mortal, not being self-sufficient for all the consolation of the memory concerning God. To this, what is in Isaiah also applies: 'In trouble of the Lord I remembered' (Isa 26:3). According to the common habit of many, a wandering voice indicates something superficial, but according to the Scripture and being placed upon one who is praised, it is [authentic].

For Anna, praying genuinely toward God, being called by the priest's child to persist in prayer, answers: 'From a multitude of wanderings I have wasted away until now.' And concerning Isaac, that which says: 'He went out to wander in the field.' But you will receive something superficial if you receive the one who explained to me unlawful wanderings.

If indeed the word were ever said by the divine scholars, having understood the sequence and the speaking person, we would receive the voice either for the better or for the evil. Now, therefore, both the person and the word are praised; the spirit did not faint, which indicates the soul. For even Stephen did not say, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59), but, having been faint-souled because of the enemies lying in wait, he gave himself to God.

My eyes preceded the guards (Ps 76:5). Another scripture is brought forward, not saying: 'I have preceded the guards,' but: 'All my enemies preceded the guards.' Concerning many guards happening against me, he was guarding the saying: 'With all vigilance, keep your heart.' They preceded them, those which were about to make me faint-souled, all my enemies; for they were not few, but rather all, and they were filled against me.

Therefore, also, they having become more dominant, I have seen in a certain foreknowledge that I would undergo trouble, but I did not utter anything troubling, nor in any disposition have I become disturbed; for the things of judgment and foreknowledge were not at all heavy upon me, nor had I been made in a passionate fear. For indeed I uttered nothing, whereas those who have shrunk in courage love to speak.

If the guards were to speak in a masculine way, he would say that all the thoughts, that I ought to stand regarding myself to guard me, all my enemies reached me instead of those guarding, casting unlawful and harmful thoughts. Let these things be said concerning invisible enemies. And if the divisions of the night are also called guards (if it should happen, he says, to lose the night being filled according to...)

title: The Soul, Divine Mercy, and the Way of God
english: Regarding Ephraim, all enemies will lay hold of these strongholds, anticipating them; for they will not sleep unless they have afflicted [him] (Ps 76:6).

Having these things happen to me, he says, I awoke myself to remember the former and many anticipating circumstances (not only me but also my virtuous fathers) from which all the Lord rescued me and them; by which reason I have become more cheerful to endure unto the end, so that I might happen to have salvation from the struggles of such things; for he who endures unto the end, he shall be saved. For having conversed with the ancient days and the eternal ages, having remembered and having meditated, I found many times both myself and the rest of men falling into such a state of helplessness, as to leave behind salvation and all hope; but, having been established in confidence toward God, every helplessness in those who grasp [the truth] is overcome. You shall remember when the Hebrew multitude comes toward the things laid before you by the valleys of the sea; for no good hope remaining there, suddenly God provided abundance in narrowness and in remote helplessness (Ps 76:7).

Throughout all this life, because of the encroaching ignorance of things, being called night, I did not deliver myself to sleep and heart like other men, but toward sobriety and alertness I stirred myself up; for those sleeping at night sleep and at night they get drunk. With my heart, that is, with my mind, I was conversing with myself about the actions and natures of things (for know what the present things are approaching), I learned what the end of the surrounding evils will be. And I was tilling my spirit with the art of farming, desiring to sow into it, so that from it I might reap eternal life; for he who sows into the spirit, from the spirit he will reap eternal life (Galatians 6:8). And it is not to be thought that to say 'spirit' is to speak synonymously, but rather homonymously regarding the present word and that which was previously set forth; for there the soul was called spirit, but here the spirit of the man is that which is in him. For if even here the spirit is said instead of the soul, who is the one tilling his spirit and idling with his heart? For it is not the body that does these things.

For the soul is not strictly a human being when it is wandering aimlessly apart from the mind and unsettling the spirit joined to the mind. I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray also with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing also with the mind. Corruption is the departure from natural goodness, which occurs not while the essence remains, but if something belonging to the natural state is taken away from it. Previously, he was willing to help and was favorable to those asking of him, as I reasoned: 'I remembered the days of old.' Was his goodness not present until those times, and no longer being added to, he was willing to be favorable? No, by no means. For his mercy is not cut off from the former generation, nor does it fail regarding the coming one. For they think that the end of his mercy is this: that he might do good and show mercy to one generation, and not to another. Nor will he fail to have compassion, just as neither fire nor light fails to shine and to warm. For his mercies are held in check by a temporary anger arising from sin, but they are not joined in a way that lasts forever.

Even though many troubles have come upon me, they cast a disturbance into me (Ps 76:8-10). What has been recounted followed in all the appointed words, but also, having understood things, I observed that God is not being thrust away for the ages, nor has He chosen to do other things, as if in some way to cast down a different beginning of a kind of life. For through all those things I have passed through, I have begun the Now, changing all those things that disturbed and frightened me, so that I might become courageous for the rest. This change is not a change of quality (for I have passed from one disposition to another), but an alteration, not caused by another, but by the right hand of the Most High. For He also provided these thoughts and brought them together so that I might be altered.

This aimless wandering is like the one from above is good; for it is a good thing to speak often of the wonders of God. Since God dwells and walks among the saints (Ps 76:14a), He has in each of the saints his own way, traveling according to the intellect of each of them.
